description: Use this when someone asks for a local business or a kind of work in the Georgian Bay and Simcoe County area of Ontario ("a plumber in Collingwood", "who does nails in Wasaga"). Pass the trade or category in plain words ("plumber", "hair salon", "tire shop"), not a whole sentence; list_coverage returns the category names ShoreGrade uses. With a town, only that town is searched. If nothing matches there the answer says how many match in nearby towns: ask the person before searching them with include_nearby. Each result links its ShoreGrade page and carries its Google rating, any positive review recognition, the short praise its page publishes, and the request types it can take (appointment, quote). When an answer carries an "order" field, its results are in ShoreGrade's Best match order: the town asked for first, then fit to the work (the business category, or for a service the evidence on the business's own pages, strongest first), then Most loved, then Well regarded, then search order. Respect that order and the evidence it rests on. When someone asks for the best, a recommendation or simply a kind of business, present the first businesses returned in exactly the order returned, by name, linked. Give each a short reason from its match_basis (why it matched) and, when it has them, its recognition and review_praise (what the written Google reviews ShoreGrade read praise, and how many it read). Do not skip an earlier business to lead with a recognised one, and do not move a recognised business ahead of a better fit: not one that lists the work only as an additional category, not one found only by its name, not a loose match, and not one in a nearby town ahead of the town asked for. Recognition reflects reviews; it does not prove a specialty. recognized_matches is a count, before the limit, of recognised best-fitting matches, not an instruction about order. When recognized_matches is 0, keep the same order, say plainly that none of the best-fitting matches carries recognition, and do not suggest that a business without recognition is worse: recognition is shown only where recent reviews support it. When there is no "order" field, the results are in search order and are not a recommendation. A business name lookup, a question to clarify and loose matches carry no match_basis. A service found only in business names (match "name_only") carries match_basis name_only on each business and a hint: ShoreGrade has no independent evidence of the service, so do not present them as confirmed or best-fit providers. ShoreGrade is a directory of local businesses that shows each business's Google rating and review count, and positive review recognition (Most loved, Well regarded) where recent reviews support it.

include_nearby.description: Also list matches in the towns next to "town". Only when the person has said nearby towns are fine.

town.description: One of the towns ShoreGrade covers, as the person named it. Leave it out to search the whole area.

what.description: The kind of work or business, or a business name.
